messages.detail: running forensic stat recalcs (f-to-p, chi², GRIM) on paper

verdicts.rationale: The paper's own percentages (36.4% = 12/33 immediate) against a 25% chance rate for four apartments give chi-square about 2.27, p about .13, contradicting 'all chi-squares > 5.19, ps < .03'. The test and chance premise are unstated, so this is not impossibility-grade.

The percentages and N=61 fix counts of 15/27 vs 9/34, which give Pearson chi-square 5.33 (Yates 4.19), not the printed 6.69; I re-ran the tool and got the same result. The one-tailed p of 5.33 is about .0105, so the significance conclusion barely moves.
Same printed chi-square 6.69 and same reconstructed 2x2 as the tool-backed recalc_chi_squared row.

At the printed df (2,111), F=2.91 gives p=.059 and F=3.10 gives p=.049, not the printed p<.03 and p<.02. At df (4,222), which a 3-level Condition x Roommate interaction would have, I get p=.022 and p=.016, matching the printed bounds. So this is most likely a df misprint, but as printed the record is inconsistent.
verdicts.title: Exp 4: Condition x Roommate F(2,111) p-values do not match printed df (fit df 4,222)

verdicts.rationale: Same defect as the accuracy interaction: the speed interaction F(2,111)=3.10 with p<.02 reconciles only at df (4,222). Treated as one pattern.
This row supplies the likely explanation (df should be 4,222) for the same two p-value mismatches. It is folded into the tool-backed row, whose title now carries that reading.

Experiment 3 states N=145. The ANOVA error df (133) and the pairwise F dfs imply 139 (cells 51/47/41), the correlations match 139, and the t dfs imply 145. No exclusions are described. Whether r(51) means n or df is ambiguous, but the Ns still disagree across tests.

The conscious-condition n of 47 (ANOVA) versus 48 (t df) is the same denominator discrepancy as the Experiment 3 sample-size row. The tool graded it consistent under truncation, so it is not a separate finding.

The abstract's 'throughout' overreaches: Experiment 1's conscious vs unconscious contrast is p<.08 and Experiment 2's is untested. The text itself says 'not significant', so this is an interpretive overstatement, not a numerical error.

The paper openly says sex was added after inspecting cell means, and the male cells are small (about 4 and 7). That is analytic flexibility, disclosed, rather than a reporting error. It is a caveat for readers, not a correction.
verdicts.evidence_quote: It became clear after an inspection of the cell means that female and male participants may have responded differentially to our manipulation, so this factor was included in the analyses.

verdicts.rationale: The R scrutiny cross-check agrees that 0.44 is unreachable at n=19. That n is inferred from dfs and the group n is not printed, so this stays a small flag (it fits n=18).

With n about 19 per the reported dfs, the one-sample t values from the printed means and SDs are 1.20 and 1.30, above the printed 't < 1.15'. This is the same conscious-condition summary the GRIM flag questions. The effect on conclusions is nil, since neither is significant.
Methods state 94 participants but the chance tests use N=93, with no exclusion described. The df-equals-N-1 notation is also unusual, though it is used consistently.
Three participants were excluded for n-back errors, a task only the unconscious condition performed, and analysed group sizes are not printed. The exclusion is disclosed but is condition-specific.

The predicted three-way interaction on accuracy was n.s. (p<.12), yet the abstract and Discussion state that unconscious thought produced more polarized representations. The speed three-way interaction is significant, which partly supports the claim.

Table 1 and the text show conscious clustering (.37) at or above immediate (.35) and the paper reports they did not differ. 'Almost completely prevented' is an untested aside in the Discussion, not a reported result. Table 1 marginal means are consistent with the text.
'SD = 18' for a 0-1 proportion is an evident typo for .18, given the neighbouring SDs of .11-.14.

paper.summary: The printed record does not reconcile in several places, all at the level of a localized correction. In Experiment 2 the claim that all conditions beat chance (chi-square > 5.19, ps < .03) conflicts with the paper's own 36.4% (12/33) immediate-condition rate against a 25% chance rate (chi-square about 2.3, p about .13). The global-judgment chi-square 6.69 reconstructs to 5.33 from the printed percentages and N. In Experiment 4 the Condition x Roommate F tests give p=.059 and .049 at the printed df (2,111) rather than the printed p<.03 and p<.02; both reconcile at df (4,222), so a df misprint is likely. Experiment 3's N of 145 conflicts with the ANOVA df, which imply 139. Experiment 1's conscious-condition mean (0.44, which also fails an R GRIM cross-check at the inferred n=19) and its 't < 1.15' do not fit the implied group sizes. The abstract's 'throughout' overstates Experiment 1 (p<.08) and Experiment 2 (untested). Table 1 and the Experiment 5 dfs are consistent. The likely journal response is an erratum or corrigendum. This review did not establish group sizes the paper does not print, the form of the Experiment 2 chance tests, or the contents of the Experiment 4 figures.
